summary.text: The seabed, also called the seafloor or ocean floor, is the bottom of the ocean.
Its structure is governed by plate tectonics, and from the deep abyssal plain it climbs toward the continents through the continental rise, slope and shelf.
Most of it is covered in layers of sediment that come from land, from living things, from chemical reactions and even from space.

facts.label: Other names
facts.value: Seafloor, sea floor, ocean floor, ocean bottom

facts.label: Most abundant sediment
facts.value: Terrigenous sediment, eroded from the continents

facts.label: Depth into the seabed
facts.value: Written as mbsf, meters below the seafloor

facts.label: How it is mapped
facts.value: Ships use acoustic technology to measure water depths

items.prompt: Tiny plankton with hard shells die near the surface, and their shells drift down and pile up on the bottom. What kind of sediment do they become?

options.label: Terrigenous, made from land
Biogenous, made by living things
Hydrogenous, made by chemical reactions
Cosmogenous, made from space

items.explain: Sediment built from the hard parts of sea creatures, such as plankton shells, is biogenous.

items.prompt: A boat heads from a beach straight out to the deep open ocean. In what order does the bottom beneath it change?

options.label: Slope, shelf, rise, then abyssal plain
Rise, slope, shelf, then abyssal plain
Abyssal plain, shelf, slope, then rise
Shelf, slope, rise, then abyssal plain

items.explain: Going from shallow to deep, the shelf drops into the slope, then the gentler rise, and finally the abyssal plain.

items.prompt: Seafloor spreading pushes up a long underwater mountain range. Where does that range run?

options.label: Through the middle of the ocean basins
Along the edges of the continents
Only beneath the polar ice caps
Just offshore from large river mouths

items.explain: Seafloor spreading creates mid-ocean ridges along the center line of major ocean basins, between the continents.

items.prompt: In volcanic areas of the deep seabed, hydrothermal vents release something into the near-freezing water around them. What?

options.label: Cold fresh water from underground rivers
Streams of molten lava and gas bubbles
Very hot, high-pressure water and chemicals
Clouds of sand and plankton shells

items.explain: Hydrothermal vents release high-pressure, extremely hot water and chemicals into the typically freezing water around them.

items.prompt: A drilling crew labels a mud sample "120 mbsf". What does that number tell you?

options.label: How deep the water was above the bottom
How far down into the seabed it was taken
How far the ship was from the nearest shore
How many years the mud took to settle

items.explain: mbsf means meters below the seafloor, a measure of depth within the seabed itself, such as down a sediment core.

items.prompt: Why does so much of the world's plastic end up in the ocean, with some sinking to the seabed?

options.label: Ships dump nearly all of it at sea
Ocean water pulls plastic in from the air
Plastic is made mostly on the coast
The world's waterways all end up in the ocean

items.explain: The ocean is the final destination for global waterways, so much of the world's plastic ends up there and some sinks.
